🇲🇽💵 <u>Peso strings together two winning weeks, closing at 18.53 per dollar</u>

The Mexican peso closed Friday at 18.53 per dollar, up 0.51% on the week and 1.44% so far in November, according to Banxico closing data reported by El Economista. Banco Base says weekly volatility fell to 5.09% from 18.19% the week before, its lowest level since mid-September. Analysts described the market's reaction to Trump's latest tariff threats against Mexico as moderate and temporary.

🇲🇽🏙️ <u>Mexico City drafts a 20-year plan so its social programs outlive any administration</u>

Mexico City's planning institute (IPDP) approved the draft 2025–2045 General Development Plan, Mayor Clara Brugada announced. 646,000 people took part in six months of public consultation, along with a free, prior and informed consultation of 84 pueblos, 44 original barrios, 75 Indigenous communities and 12 Afro-descendant organizations. The goals include a childcare center within 15 minutes of every home, all-electric public transport, an end to extreme poverty, and no neighborhood without water, drainage, parks, schools or clinics. "This plan doesn't belong to a party. It belongs to the city and its people," Brugada said.

🇲🇽📺 <u>90% of Mexico's radio and TV broadcasters now have ethics codes and audience ombudspersons</u>

More than 90% of Mexico's commercial and public radio and TV licensees now have codes of ethics and audience defenders, the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission (CRT) reports. The deadline closed November 6 under the audience-rights guidelines published in the DOF on August 28. From November 16, viewers and listeners can file complaints. The codes must cover non-discrimination and the prevention of hate speech and violence, plus news standards requiring minimum grounds to consider a story truthful before it airs.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Sheinbaum opens a joint review with INEGI of 2025 homicide figures</u>

The federal government and INEGI have set up a working group to reconcile 2025 homicide numbers. The Security Cabinet's figures come from case files opened by state prosecutors and the FGR, while INEGI's come from death certificates and civil registries. "INEGI gives a preliminary figure and then its definitive figure. Between the two, there was a bigger difference than in previous years," Sheinbaum said. The group is going state by state to find where the two counts diverge.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Ebrard: no free-trade deal with China in the short term. Mexico goes to APEC for stable rules</u>

"A free-trade treaty is not planned in the short term," Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said when asked about China, ahead of Sheinbaum's trip to the APEC summit in Shenzhen. In Shenzhen, Mexico will push for greater stability and predictability in trade rules, and it is aiming for agreements with Asia-Pacific economies in 2027 and 2028. Ebrard noted that Beijing is more open to free trade than an increasingly protectionist Washington, which still accounts for more than 80% of Mexico's trade.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Mexico's measles outbreak is down to six active cases</u>

At its peak, Mexico was confirming 1,314 measles cases a week. As of November 12, the Health Ministry counts six active cases: five in Chiapas and one in Quintana Roo. The outbreak that began in 2025 left 20,552 confirmed cases and 50 deaths across all 32 states. Health Secretary David Kershenobich reports 90% vaccination coverage and 40.9 million doses applied, with a target of 95% within three months.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>Mexico's tourism revenue reaches $26.1 billion through September</u>

From January to September, Mexico took in $26.096 billion in tourism revenue, up 1.4% from 2025, INEGI reports, and 35,975,580 international tourists arrived, up 3.8%. September alone brought $1.94 billion from international visitors, up 5.7%, and spending by air arrivals grew 8.2%. Air arrivals, which bring in about 80% of the revenue, are still down 4.3% for the year. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Passenger trains return: construction toward Guadalajara starts in December</u>

The Transport Ministry (SICT) says construction on the Irapuato–Guadalajara stretch of the Mexico City–Guadalajara passenger train officially starts in December, with a groundbreaking in Silao, Guanajuato. The army's "Felipe Ángeles" military engineers will build the line to Zapopan with five stations, and two more are under evaluation. The federal rail agency has signed agreements with Jalisco and the municipalities along the route to clear the right of way. Neoliberal governments shut down passenger rail in the 1990s.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Córdova and Jacobo's INE payouts were "immoral"</u>

Former INE president Lorenzo Córdova left with a severance of about 11 million pesos, and ex-executive secretary Edmundo Jacobo Molina with about 13 million. "It may be legal, but what the councilors gave themselves is also immoral: 11 and 13 million pesos for leaving the INE," Sheinbaum said. They "earned 2 million pesos a month gross, and then they take 11 million." She asked the ASF and the FGR to look into the supplier monopoly behind electoral materials, which no administration dismantled, and proposed that the state-owned Talleres Gráficos produce them.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>In Mexico, the richest 0.1% pollute as much as the poorest 40%</u>

A new Oxfam México report, released ahead of COP31, finds that about 128,000 people, the richest 0.1%, emit as much as roughly 50 million Mexicans in the bottom 40%. Mexico's ultra-rich average 267.9 tons of CO2 per person per year, more than their European peers (236.6) and the OECD's (256.05). Mexico's poorest 10% emit 0.5 tons. "The ultra-rich in Mexico are the ones who pollute the most," Oxfam researcher Ervin Félix López told Contralínea.
